title: Ransomware on office PCs
scenario: A phishing email or bad download encrypts PCs and the backup USB drive that stays plugged in.
recommendation: Keep one backup copy offline or in immutable cloud storage, test a restore every quarter, and turn on antivirus alert forwarding to the MSP.

title: Email account takeover
scenario: An attacker phishes a staff password and logs into email with no MFA to read patient messages or send fake invoices.
recommendation: Turn on MFA for every email account and run phishing awareness training twice a year.

title: Unpatched imaging PC
scenario: The Windows 10 X-ray imaging PC has updates turned off and sits on the same network as everything else.
recommendation: Put the imaging PC on its own network segment, ask the imaging vendor for a supported OS path, and add it to the asset inventory.

title: Lost or stolen laptop
scenario: A provider's laptop with patient files saved locally is lost. The drive is not encrypted so it counts as a reportable breach.
recommendation: Turn on BitLocker for all laptops and stop saving patient files locally.

title: Shared front desk login
scenario: Several staff use one account so there is no way to tell who looked at or changed a patient record.
recommendation: Give each staff member their own login and write a short password and access policy.

title: Former employee access
scenario: An ex-employee's accounts stay active after they leave.
recommendation: Add account removal to the offboarding checklist and review active accounts every quarter.

title: MSP or vendor compromise
scenario: An attacker gets into the MSP's remote management tool or the cloud practice management vendor and reaches the office from there.
recommendation: Ask both vendors for security documentation, add security terms to the MSP contract, and require MFA on the MSP's remote access.

title: Breach goes unnoticed
scenario: An intruder is in the network for weeks because nobody reviews logs or alerts.
recommendation: Send firewall, sign-in and antivirus alerts to the MSP and review a weekly summary. Tools like a simple auth log analyzer can automate the first pass.

title: Disorganized incident response
scenario: During an incident staff don't know who to call, what to unplug, or what HIPAA requires them to report.
recommendation: Write a one-page incident response plan with contacts, first steps, and HIPAA notification requirements, then run a tabletop exercise once a year.

title: Internet outage
scenario: The single internet connection goes down and the cloud practice management system is unreachable.
recommendation: Accept for now. Keep a printed day schedule as a fallback and revisit a backup connection next budget cycle.
